newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks extend slide amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks extend slide amid profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks were extending their early losses at midday Monday amid light profit-taking and cautiousness ahead of next Sunday's midterm elections, traders said.

"The market looks a little skittish, with elections, the U.S. (Federal Reserve) meeting and a U.S. market holiday coming up," a desk trader said, referring to the Fed's policy meeting starting Tuesday and the July 4th holiday on Friday.
The leading IPC share index was down 56.98 points, or 1.27 percent, at 4,424.13.
Trading volume was thin at 22.6 million shares.

Traders said scant volume suggested a sell-off was not under way. "Dealers are not doing much, except watch the market. They are most likely letting it trickle down to step in and buy low at a later stage," the trader added.

Mexican voters will go to the polls on July 6 to elect all members of the lower chamber of Congress, one quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time in modern history, the mayor of Mexico City.
The Fed's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee will meet to review interest rates on Tuesday and Wednesday,
Dealers said most U.S. players were likely to be absent from Mexican markets on Friday because of the Independence Day holiday.
Financial group Bancomer weighed most on the market on Monday, traders said. The stock, the most active blue chip among the decliners, was down 1 centavo to 2.28 pesos.
On the broad market, decliners outnumbered gainers by 49 to 14, among the 79 issues that changed hands.
